Rep. Erin Paré criticizes Wake County School Board over education funding decisions
M. P. Welch
Rep. Erin Paré, a Republican elected to the North Carolina State House in 2021 representing the 37th district, has recently posted several statements on her Twitter account regarding local education funding and her background as a small business owner.
On August 16, 2026, Paré shared personal details about her family's investment in their community, writing: "Wayne and I are local small business owners. Back in 2017 we decided to invest our savings in a local small business that helped local families afford youth sports equipment for their kids. We wanted to invest in a community after moving a lot as an Army family. But starting a".
Three days later, on August 19, 2026, Paré addressed recent decisions by the Wake County School Board and contrasted them with actions taken by the state legislature. She stated, "Last night the Democrat-led Wake County School Board cut teacher pay. The Republican-led state legislature passed the largest veteran and starting teacher pay raise in decades. #ncpol https://t.co/tA1arWH909".
Later that same day, she commented on funding for students with disabilities: "I guess the Democrats were just joking when they said they wanted to increase funding for students with disabilities. The Republican-led state budget was so strong on funding our students, the Democrat-led Wake County School Board approved over $4million in cuts for students https://t.co/RWL23DqwcN".
Paré succeeded Sydney Batch when she was elected to represent North Carolina's 37th House district. Her recent posts highlight ongoing debates between state and local officials over education funding priorities and fiscal policy within Wake County schools.
